checks.title: Hunters come before armour
checks.model: mobile predators by 558 Ma; skeletons spread at 532 Ma
checks.real: bore holes in Cloudina tubes about 550 Ma, before the small shelly fossils from 538 Ma

checks.title: Skeletons come before sharp eyes
checks.model: skeletons spread at 532 Ma; eyes with lenses at 522 Ma
checks.real: skeletons from 550 Ma (Cloudina) and 538 Ma (small shelly fossils); the oldest eyes about 530 to 521 Ma
checks.source: Kouchinsky et al. 2012; Schoenemann et al. 2017

checks.title: When skeletons spread
checks.real: small shelly fossils diversify from 538 to about 525 Ma (accept 545 to 525)
checks.source: Kouchinsky et al. 2012; Maloof et al. 2010

checks.title: When eyes with lenses appear
checks.real: compound eyes of trilobites and radiodonts, about 530 to 515 Ma (accept 535 to 512)
checks.source: Schoenemann et al. 2017; Paterson et al. 2011

checks.title: At Burgess Shale time, arthropods are the richest group
checks.model: 32 % of species are arthropods; the richest group is arthropods
checks.real: arthropods are the largest group in the Burgess Shale, about 37 % of its species

checks.title: Body plans spread out fast
checks.model: disparity at 508 Ma is 4.7 times that at 550 Ma
checks.real: by the Burgess Shale, Cambrian arthropods alone were as varied in form as living ones (accept 2 times or more)
checks.source: Briggs, Fortey & Wills 1992; Erwin et al. 2011

checks.title: Microbial mats give way to churned mud
checks.model: mats cover 90 % of the floor at 550 Ma and 55 % at 508 Ma
checks.real: mats cover Ediacaran sea floors; burrowers break them up through the Cambrian (accept at least 70 % before, at most 60 % after)

checks.title: The biggest hunter at Burgess Shale time
checks.real: Anomalocaris canadensis grew to about 30 to 40 cm; most Cambrian hunters were far smaller (accept 8 to 100 cm)

checks.title: Without predators, no explosion
checks.model: disparity 0.44 against 0.83; skeletons on 0 % of animals, eyes on 0 %
checks.real: the arms-race view: predation drove armour, eyes and the spread of body plans (accept disparity below 60 % of the default, armour and eyes under 10 %)

checks.title: Low oxygen holds the explosion back
checks.model: at 525 Ma: disparity 0.23 against 0.53, mats 88 % against 56 %
checks.real: active hunting and deep burrowing need more oxygen than Ediacaran seas held (accept disparity lower and mats higher than the default)

checks.title: If eyes had come first, the fossil order would be reversed
checks.model: with cheap early eyes: eyes with lenses at 535 Ma, skeletons at 534 Ma
checks.real: the record shows skeletons before eyes, so eyes alone did not start the arms race (Parker’s light switch, as first dated)
